concepts.why: Secular/Jewish scholar, Reformed, Orthodox: the name says the LORD founded the earth BY wisdom. Job 28:25-27 says God looked at wisdom and appraised it when He made wind and water; it does not say the earth was founded by wisdom. It belongs under 'Where can wisdom be found?' (28:23 is already there).

Secular scholar, Baptist: the name is the LORD giving and taking away. Eccl 5:15 and 1 Tim 6:7 say only that a man leaves with nothing; neither names the LORD as giver or taker. The half of Job 1:21 they echo ('naked I came') is not what the name says. Eccl 7:14 stays.

Secular scholar, Reformed: the name is Job's charge against the friends. Job 15:2 is Eliphaz charging Job with empty counsel, the reverse direction, and says nothing about comforting; it makes the group read as if both sides were 'miserable comforters'.

Secular scholar, Wesleyan: the name is a question put to the LORD ('How long'). Job 3:1-3 is a curse on the day of his birth, with no address to the LORD and no 'how long'; it shares a mood, not the cry.

concepts.name: Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
concepts.why: Secular scholar, Lutheran: the name is Job 5:13 (Eliphaz speaking) and says God catches the wise in craftiness; 1 Cor 1:25 and 1:27 (God's foolishness wiser; God chose the foolish to shame the wise) and Ps 94:11 do not say that. 1 Cor 1:20 states the shared claim in the texts' own words and is already in the packet; Job 5:13, 3:19, Isa 29:14, Ps 94:11 all fit it.
